Fit one linear model per feature and test coefficients, and contrasts, with limma's moderated t

stats_fit.Rd

Fit one linear model per feature of a feature-by-sample table and test each named coefficient, and each contrast of a contrasts file with its confidence interval, with limma's empirical-Bayes moderated t, Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted, in one call.

Runs mzLib's LinearModel.Fit once - every design column is fitted - and then EmpiricalBayes.Moderate for each coefficient you name, which also applies Benjamini-Hochberg across that coefficient's fitted features. This is limma's lmFit() then eBayes(legacy = TRUE) (Smyth 2004), which mzLib holds to limma to 1e-8 relative on limma's own reference output. With contrasts, EmpiricalBayes.ModerateContrasts also tests each row of a contrasts file - "250 ng against 125 ng", "the mean of two groups against a third" - with its confidence interval: limma's contrasts.fit() then eBayes() then topTable(confint = ...).

Usage

stats_fit(responses, design, coefficients = character(0), contrasts = NULL,
  confidence = NULL, estimator = NULL, trend = FALSE, spline_basis = NULL, threads = 1,
  timeout = 600)

Arguments

responses

A TSV with a header row. First column the feature id; every other column one sample, named by its header. Use the values as you want them modelled - log2 intensities, usually. Blank, NA or NaN is missing and left out of that feature's fit, never imputed; 0 is an observation, so blank out any 0 that means "not measured".

design

A TSV with a header row and one row per sample: first column the sample name (matching the responses header exactly, in any order), then one numeric column per coefficient. Include an intercept column yourself if you want one. diff_design writes one (design_<i>.tsv) from a sample sheet.

coefficients

Design column names to test, each with its own moderated test and its own Benjamini-Hochberg family. May be empty (character(0)) when you give contrasts.

contrasts

A TSV of contrasts, as diff_design writes it beside the design (contrasts_<i>.tsv): a header of the contrast id column, then exactly the design's coefficient columns (in any order); then one row per contrast, its id and one weight per coefficient, e.g. -1 and 1 for the second level minus the first. Each contrast gets its own moderated test, Benjamini-Hochberg family and confidence interval, in contrasts. NULL sends none. Needs the pyMzLib 0.6.0 bridge.

confidence

The two-sided level of the contrasts' intervals, as a fraction (0 to 1), strictly between 0 and 1; only with contrasts. Leave it NULL for mzLib's default (0.95 at mzLib d10017ce); contrasts$confidence_level says which level was used.

estimator

How the variance prior is estimated, one of "moments_legacy" (limma's eBayes(legacy = TRUE)) or "marginal_likelihood" (mzLib's own estimator, which uses each feature's own residual degrees of freedom, so it handles the unequal df that missing values cause exactly). Leave it NULL for mzLib's default ("moments_legacy" at mzLib d10017ce); prior$estimator says which was used.

trend

Let the prior variance follow average response (limma's trend = TRUE), for data whose low-abundance features are noisier.

spline_basis

Basis functions of the trend spline, intercept included. Only with trend = TRUE. Leave it NULL to let mzLib choose, as limma does, for the number of features; mzLib may also use fewer than you ask for. Either way prior$spline_basis_count reports what it used.

threads

Features fitted at once (threads), or -1 for every core. The answer is identical at any value.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Details

A feature is fitted on the samples where it was observed, and is reported - never dropped - when it cannot be: "too_few_observations" when it has no more observed samples than the design has coefficients, "rank_deficient" when its observed samples cannot separate the coefficients (a feature seen in only one group cannot have a group effect).

Value

An mzlibr_moderated_fit:

- records, a data.frame with one row per (tested coefficient, feature) - one block of feature_count rows per coefficient, in the order you named them, and no rows when you named none - with feature, coefficient, status, estimate (response units per coefficient unit: a log2 fold change for a 0/1 group column on log2 intensities), standard_error (response units per coefficient unit), t (standard errors), df_total (degrees of freedom), p_value and bh_adjusted (fractions, 0 to 1), posterior_variance and prior_variance (squared response units), sigma (response units), df_residual, observed (samples) and average_response (response units). Statistics are NA where status is not "fitted". - responses_file, design_file and contrasts_file (NA when you gave no contrasts), as absolute paths; feature_count features and sample_count samples read; sample_names, coefficient_names (every design column, in the order each contrast's weights follow) and tested_coefficients (empty when you named none); missing_count and zero_count response cells; status_counts, features per status; threads; row_count rows. - residual_df_differ: TRUE when the fitted features do not all have the same residual degrees of freedom. Then default limma (3.61 and later) uses a different prior estimator and reports different moderated statistics; under "moments_legacy" these are legacy = TRUE, and estimator = "marginal_likelihood" is mzLib's estimator for this case. - prior, the fitted variance prior, shared by every coefficient and contrast: estimator, the estimator used (NA only from a bridge before pyMzLib 0.6.0, which did not report it); df (degrees of freedom, NA when infinite; under "marginal_likelihood" mzLib searches d0 from about 0.05 upward, so a d0 there is that floor, not an optimum), df_infinite, trended, spline_basis_count (basis functions) and scale (squared response units), s0^2 when every fitted feature shares one. scale is NA when it differs by feature, which is then in the prior_variance column: with a trend, or with fewer than 3 features. Then mzLib fits no prior (mzLib #1398, as limma's squeezeVar does): df is 0 and each feature keeps its own variance. Bridges before pyMzLib 0.6.0 report the first feature's own variance as scale in that case. - contrasts, NULL when you gave no contrasts; otherwise an mzlibr_moderated_contrasts: confidence_level, the two-sided level of every interval as a fraction (0 to 1); tested_contrasts, the contrast ids in the file's order; weights, a list from contrast id to its weights (contrast weight per coefficient, unitless), one per coefficient_names entry, whatever order the file's columns were in; row_count rows, feature_count x the contrasts; column_names; and records, one row per (contrast, feature), a block per contrast in file order, with feature, contrast (its id), status, estimate (response units per contrast unit: a log2 fold change for one level against another on log2 intensities), standard_error, confidence_low and confidence_high (response units per contrast unit; the two-sided confidence_level interval, not adjusted across features), and the coefficient table's t, df_total, p_value, bh_adjusted (over this contrast's fitted features), posterior_variance, prior_variance, sigma, df_residual, observed and average_response, in the same units. Statistics are NA where status is not "fitted". - caveats, including any that apply to this input: the estimator, unfitted features, zeros, residual_df_differ, contrasts.

What it is not

By default it is limma's *legacy* estimator; estimator = "marginal_likelihood" is mzLib's own, close to default limma's but not equal. robust = TRUE, the B-statistic and observation weights are not implemented. With missing values a contrast's standard error is exact per feature, where limma's contrasts.fit() approximates it, so on such data the contrasts differ from limma's by design. bh_adjusted controls the false discovery rate among the features tested; it is not a target-decoy q-value.

Bridges before pyMzLib 0.6.0

Such a bridge has stats fit but ignores --contrasts, --confidence and --estimator. Rather than return a fit that silently did not do what you asked, stats_fit() raises an mzlib_usage_error naming the 0.6.0 bridge when you gave contrasts or estimator and the answer lacks what they add.

Wraps

Wire verb stats fit. Generated from the bridge's verb spec stats.fit.yaml (bridge commit 45833ca804d6) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

responses

path; required. A TSV with a header row. The first column is the feature id (unique, any header); every other column is one sample, named by its header. Cells are used as given, so log-transform intensities first. A blank cell, NA or NaN (any case) is missing and is omitted from that feature's fit, never imputed. A 0 is an OBSERVATION. Blank lines are skipped.

design

path; required. A TSV with a header row and one row per sample. The first column is the sample name and must match the responses header exactly (rows are matched by name, so their order does not matter); every other column is one coefficient, named by its header, and every cell must be a finite number. The design is used as written: include an intercept column if you want one. diff design --out writes one (design_i.tsv).

coefficients (wire --stdin)

string[]; default absent; range >= 1 line, or none with --contrasts; each a design column name, none repeated. The coefficients to test, one design column name per line. Each gets its own moderated test and its own Benjamini-Hochberg family. The model always fits every design column. With --contrasts it may be empty, and the coefficient table then has no rows.

contrasts

path; default absent. A TSV of contrasts to test, as diff design --out writes it (contrasts_i.tsv, beside its design_i.tsv). A header row: the contrast id column (any header; diff design writes contrast), then exactly the design's coefficient columns, matched by name, so in any order. Then one row per contrast: a non-empty id (diff design's c1, c2, ...), then one finite weight per coefficient; the contrast is the weighted sum of the coefficients, e.g. -1 and 1 for the second minus the first. A design column the file lacks, or a column the design lacks, is refused. mzLib refuses a contrast whose weights are all 0, and two contrasts with one id. Each contrast is moderated with the same prior as the coefficients (EmpiricalBayes.ModerateContrasts) and has its own Benjamini-Hochberg family; its rows are the contrasts table. Absent, there is no contrasts table. Needs the pyMzLib 0.6.0 bridge; an older bridge ignores the option.

confidence

float; in fraction (0 to 1); default absent; range strictly between 0 and 1 (mzLib's rule); only with --contrasts. The two-sided level of each contrast's confidence interval. Absent, the bridge sends none and ModerateContrasts' own default applies (confidenceLevel = 0.95 at d10017ce); contrasts.confidence_level reports the level used either way. A value mzLib refuses is a usage error with mzLib's message. Needs the pyMzLib 0.6.0 bridge.

estimator

string; default absent; range moments_legacy | marginal_likelihood. How the variance prior (d0, s0^2) is estimated, mzLib's VariancePriorEstimator by a wire name. moments_legacy is MomentsLegacy: the method of moments on log variances (Smyth 2004), limma's eBayes(legacy = TRUE), exact when every feature has the same residual df. marginal_likelihood is MarginalLikelihood: maximum marginal likelihood with each feature's own residual df, which handles the unequal df that omitting missing values causes exactly (mzLib #1368); it is mzLib's own estimator, not limma's default fitFDistUnequalDF1, so its numbers are close to default limma's but not equal. The one estimator serves the coefficients and the contrasts. Absent, the bridge sends none and mzLib's default applies (MomentsLegacy at d10017ce, kept for limma legacy parity); prior.estimator reports the estimator used either way. Needs the pyMzLib 0.6.0 bridge.

trend

flag; default FALSE. Let the prior variance trend with each feature's average response (limma's trend = TRUE), as a natural cubic spline.

spline_basis (wire --spline-basis)

int; in basis functions; default absent; range >= 1; only with --trend. Basis functions of the trend spline, intercept included. Absent, the bridge sends none and mzLib chooses by limma's fitFDist rule (EmpiricalBayes.DefaultSplineBasisCount, mzLib 1.0.594 #1398): 1 + (n >= 3) + (n >= 6) + (n >= 30) for n fitted features, so 4 only from 30 features. A given value is capped at the fitted features minus one. mzLib caps either at the distinct average responses and may merge coinciding knots; prior.spline_basis_count reports what was used.

threads

int; in threads; default 1; range >= 1, or -1 for every core. Features fitted at once. The bridge default is 1 (BULK.md); mzLib's own default is -1. Results are identical at any value.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

responses_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the responses table.

design_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the design table.

contrasts_file

string; NA when no --contrasts was given. Absolute path of the contrasts table. Absent from bridges before pyMzLib 0.6.0 (optional forever).

feature_count

int; in features; never NA. Feature rows read.

sample_count

int; in samples; never NA. Sample columns read.

sample_names

string[]; never NA. In responses header order, which is the order the design rows were put in.

coefficient_names

string[]; never NA. Every design column, in order: the order of each contrast's weights.

tested_coefficients

string[]; never NA. The stdin coefficients, in order; the table holds one block of feature_count rows per entry. Empty when only --contrasts was given.

trend

bool; never NA. Whether --trend was given.

threads

int; in threads; never NA. The thread count used.

missing_count

int; in cells; never NA. Response cells that were blank, NA or NaN.

zero_count

int; in cells; never NA. Response cells that are exactly 0, fitted as observations.

status_counts

map<string,int>; in features; never NA. Features per status: fitted, too_few_observations, rank_deficient.

residual_df_differ

bool; never NA. True when the fitted features do not all have the same residual df (missing values omitted). Then default limma (>= 3.61, eBayes legacy = FALSE) would use a different prior estimator and report different moderated statistics; under moments_legacy these follow legacy = TRUE, and marginal_likelihood is mzLib's estimator for this case. A caveat says so.

prior

object; never NA. The fitted variance prior, shared by every tested coefficient and contrast; fields under result.tables.prior.

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. feature_count x the number of tested coefficients.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The coefficient table's columns, in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. One row per (tested coefficient, feature): coefficient blocks in stdin order, features in file order. The same with or without --contrasts.

contrasts

object; NA when no --contrasts was given. The tested contrasts, as a second table beside the coefficient table: fields under result.tables.contrasts, its rows' columns under result.tables.contrasts.columns. A separate table because a contrast row is keyed by a contrast id and carries a confidence interval, which a coefficient row has neither of; one table holding both would leave half of every row's keys null, and the coefficient table stays as it was without --contrasts. Absent from bridges before pyMzLib 0.6.0 (optional forever).

caveats

string[]; never NA. Three static caveats (the first names the prior estimator), plus one each when residual_df_differ, when any feature was not fitted (with counts), when any cell is 0, and when the prior df is infinite; and two more with --contrasts.

Columns of records

feature

string; never NA. The feature id from the responses file's first column.

coefficient

string; never NA. The coefficient this row tests.

status

string; never NA. fitted | too_few_observations (fewer observed samples than coefficients plus one) | rank_deficient (the design restricted to this feature's observed samples is not of full rank). Only fitted rows carry statistics or enter the BH family.

estimate

float; in response units per coefficient unit (e.g. log2 fold change for a 0/1 group column on log2 intensities); NA when status is not fitted. The least-squares coefficient; moderation does not change it.

standard_error

float; in response units per coefficient unit; NA when not fitted. Moderated standard error: sqrt(posterior_variance) x the coefficient's unscaled standard deviation.

t

float; in standard errors; NA when not fitted. Moderated t-statistic.

df_total

float; in degrees of freedom; NA when not fitted. Degrees of freedom of the moderated t: df_residual + prior df, capped at the pooled residual df.

p_value

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when not fitted. Two-sided p-value.

bh_adjusted

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when not fitted (not in the family). Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value over this coefficient's fitted features. Not a target-decoy q-value.

posterior_variance

float; in squared response units; NA when not fitted. The moderated residual variance (d0 s0^2 + d s^2) / (d0 + d).

prior_variance

float; in squared response units; NA when not fitted (the feature did not enter the prior). s0^2 for this feature: one value for every feature without --trend, varying with average_response with it. With fewer than 3 features it is the feature's own variance, because no prior is fitted.

sigma

float; in response units; NA when not fitted. Residual standard deviation, sqrt(RSS / df_residual), before moderation.

df_residual

int; NA when not fitted. Observed samples minus coefficients.

observed

int; in samples; never NA. Samples with a finite response for this feature.

average_response

float; in response units; NA when the feature has no finite response at all. Mean of the feature's observed responses: the covariate --trend fits on.

Fields of prior

prior$estimator (wire estimator)

string; never NA. moments_legacy or marginal_likelihood: the estimator mzLib reports it fitted the prior with (VariancePrior.Estimator), its default when --estimator was absent. Absent from bridges before pyMzLib 0.6.0.

prior$df (wire df)

float; in degrees of freedom; NA when infinite: df_infinite is true. Prior degrees of freedom d0. 0 with fewer than 3 features, where mzLib fits no prior (mzLib#1398, as limma's squeezeVar), so moderation leaves each feature's variance and t as they are. Under marginal_likelihood mzLib searches d0 from about 0.05 (e^-3) upward, so a d0 there is the search's floor, not an optimum.

prior$df_infinite (wire df_infinite)

bool; never NA. True when the residual variances are no more dispersed than sampling alone explains, so every feature takes the prior variance.

prior$trended (wire trended)

bool; never NA. Whether s0^2 varies with average_response.

prior$spline_basis_count (wire spline_basis_count)

int; in basis functions; never NA. Basis functions the trend used, intercept included; 1 without a trend.

prior$scale (wire scale)

float; in squared response units; NA when s0^2 differs by feature, so it is in the prior_variance column: trended, or no prior was fitted (fewer than 3 features; mzLib#1398, as limma's squeezeVar). s0^2, the prior variance, when every fitted feature shares one. With fewer than 3 features mzLib fits no prior: df is 0 and each feature keeps its own variance. Bridges before pyMzLib 0.6.0 reported the first feature's own variance here in that case.

Fields of contrasts

contrasts$confidence_level (wire confidence_level)

float; in fraction (0 to 1); never NA. The two-sided level of every confidence_low and confidence_high: --confidence, or mzLib's default when it was absent (ModeratedContrast.ConfidenceLevel).

contrasts$tested_contrasts (wire tested_contrasts)

string[]; never NA. The contrast ids, in file order; the table holds one block of feature_count rows per entry.

contrasts$weights (wire weights)

map<string,float[]>; in contrast weight per coefficient (unitless); never NA. Each contrast id's weights, one per coefficient_names entry, in that order (the file's columns matched by name): what mzLib tested.

contrasts$row_count (wire row_count)

int; in rows; never NA. feature_count x the number of contrasts.

contrasts$column_names (wire column_names)

string[]; never NA. The contrasts table's columns, in order (result.tables.contrasts.columns).

contrasts$records (wire columns)

table; never NA. One row per (contrast, feature): contrast blocks in file order, features in file order.

Fields of contrasts.columns

feature

string; never NA. The feature id from the responses file's first column.

contrast

string; never NA. The contrast id this row tests, from the contrasts file's first column. diff design numbers its contrasts within each stratum; its label column says what each id compares.

status

string; never NA. The feature's fit status, as in the coefficient table. Only fitted rows carry statistics or enter the contrast's BH family.

estimate

float; in response units per contrast unit (e.g. log2 fold change for a level-against-level contrast on log2 intensities); NA when not fitted. The contrast's least-squares estimate, the weighted sum of the coefficients; moderation does not change it.

standard_error

float; in response units per contrast unit; NA when not fitted. Moderated standard error: sqrt(posterior_variance) x sqrt(c'(X'X)^-1 c), with the feature's own (X'X)^-1 over its observed samples.

confidence_low

float; in response units per contrast unit; NA when not fitted. Lower bound of the two-sided confidence_level interval: estimate - t-quantile((1 + level) / 2, df_total) x standard_error. Per feature, not adjusted across features.

confidence_high

float; in response units per contrast unit; NA when not fitted. Upper bound: estimate + the same half-width.

t

float; in standard errors; NA when not fitted. Moderated t-statistic.

df_total

float; in degrees of freedom; NA when not fitted. df_residual + prior df, capped at the pooled residual df, as for a coefficient.

p_value

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when not fitted. Two-sided p-value.

bh_adjusted

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when not fitted (not in the family). Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-value over this contrast's fitted features. Not a target-decoy q-value.

posterior_variance

float; in squared response units; NA when not fitted. The moderated residual variance, as in the coefficient table.

prior_variance

float; in squared response units; NA when not fitted (the feature did not enter the prior). s0^2 for this feature, as in the coefficient table.

sigma

float; in response units; NA when not fitted. Residual standard deviation before moderation.

df_residual

int; NA when not fitted. Observed samples minus coefficients.

observed

int; in samples; never NA. Samples with a finite response for this feature.

average_response

float; in response units; NA when the feature has no finite response at all. Mean of the feature's observed responses.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

responses, design or contrasts missing, blank or not found (or --contrasts without a value); a table empty, header-only or with too few columns; a row whose field count differs from its header; an empty or repeated feature id, sample, coefficient name or contrasts column; a response cell that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN); a design cell or contrast weight that is not a finite number

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

the design's samples are not exactly the responses' sample columns, or the contrasts file's columns are not exactly the design's coefficients (both differences are named); an empty contrast id; no coefficient on stdin without --contrasts, one named twice, or one not in the design; --spline-basis without --trend, or below 1; --confidence without --contrasts, without a value or not a number; --estimator other than moments_legacy or marginal_likelihood, or without a value; --threads 0 or below -1

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib refuses the input (its ArgumentException, reclassified, with mzLib's message): the design is not of full column rank; fewer than 2 features could be fitted, so no variance prior exists; a contrast whose weights are all 0; two contrasts with one id; a confidence level not strictly between 0 and 1

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • Under the default estimator, moments_legacy, this is limma's LEGACY empirical-Bayes estimator (eBayes(legacy = TRUE)). Since limma 3.61, eBayes defaults to a different estimator whenever residual df differ between features, which omitting missing values causes; residual_df_differ says when that applies. For that case mzLib offers marginal_likelihood, which handles unequal df exactly (VariancePriorEstimator.MarginalLikelihood, 'this library's answer to that gap' in mzLib's EmpiricalBayes docs). It is mzLib's own estimator, not limma's fitFDistUnequalDF1, so its numbers differ from default limma's too; mzLib keeps moments_legacy the default for limma legacy parity.

  • Not implemented: robust = TRUE, the B-statistic, observation weights.

  • Contrasts (--contrasts) use the same prior as the coefficients, and each has its own Benjamini-Hochberg family. confidence_low and confidence_high are per feature, not adjusted across features. With missing values a contrast's standard error is exact per feature, where limma's contrasts.fit approximates it, so on such data the contrasts differ from limma's by design; with complete data they agree, and a contrast of one coefficient gives exactly that coefficient's row.

  • A 0 is an observation. Log-transform intensities first, and blank any cell that means 'not measured'.

  • bh_adjusted adjusts for the false discovery rate among the features tested. It is not a target-decoy q-value for identifications.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.stats.fit

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::stats::fit_with with FitOptions

  • R (mzLibR): stats_fit

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.3.0; mzLibRust not yet shipped; mzLibR not yet shipped.

  • doi:10.1093/nar/gkv007: limma, whose eBayes(legacy = TRUE), and contrasts.fit with topTable(confint), mzLib reproduces to 1e-8 relative (Ritchie et al., Nucleic Acids Res 43:e47, 2015)

  • doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x: the Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment in bh_adjusted (J R Stat Soc B 57:289, 1995)

See also

diff_design, which writes the design and contrasts files; stats_adjust, stats_meta, stats_fit_mixed for samples in groups

Examples


# A dilution series from mzLib's own RNA test data: MALAT1 at 500, 250 and 125 ng against a
# constant FLuc spike, log2 intensities normalised to FLuc. Halving MALAT1 should read as about -1.
data <- system.file("extdata", "stats", package = "mzLibR")
fit <- stats_fit(file.path(data, "malat_dilution_log2_vs_fluc.tsv"),
  file.path(data, "malat_dilution_design.tsv"), c("malat_250ng", "malat_125ng"))
fit
#> <mzlibr_moderated_fit> 492 features x 27 samples, testing malat_250ng, malat_125ng
#>   fitted 212, too_few_observations 214, rank_deficient 66
#>   prior df 19.56 (moments_legacy)
#>   ! residual df differ between features: these are eBayes(legacy = TRUE) statistics
fit$status_counts
#>               fitted too_few_observations       rank_deficient 
#>                  212                  214                   66 
c(estimator = fit$prior$estimator, prior_df = round(fit$prior$df, 1))
#>        estimator         prior_df 
#> "moments_legacy"           "19.6" 
malat <- fit$records[fit$records$coefficient == "malat_250ng" & fit$records$status == "fitted" &
  startsWith(fit$records$feature, "MALAT1:"), ]
c(oligos = nrow(malat), median_log2_fold_change = median(malat$estimate))
#>                  oligos median_log2_fold_change 
#>             116.0000000              -0.8914901 

# Every pair of loads, with intervals: diff_design() with no reference level writes one contrast
# per pair beside the design, and `contrasts` tests them all.
samples <- system.file("extdata", "diff", "malat_dilution_samples.tsv", package = "mzLibR")
design <- diff_design(samples, factors = list(factor_spec("malat_load")),
  out = file.path(tempdir(), "malat_pairs"))
stratum <- design$strata[[1]]
pairs <- stats_fit(file.path(data, "malat_dilution_log2_vs_fluc.tsv"), stratum$design_file,
  contrasts = stratum$contrasts_file)
pairs$contrasts
#> <mzlibr_moderated_contrasts> 3 contrast(s) x 492 features, 95% intervals
#>   c1: 0 1 0
#>   c2: 0 0 1
#>   c3:  0 -1  1
pairs$contrasts$weights$c3
#> [1]  0 -1  1
pairs$coefficient_names
#> [1] "intercept"        "malat_load=250ng" "malat_load=500ng"
